stories.title: Show HN: Isometric SF – A pixel-art map of the SF Bay Area
summary: It's really fun to explore and stumble upon various famous landmarks like Apple Park, Palace of Fine Arts, or UC Berkeley.The technicals involve using Nano Banana 2 to train a Qwen-Image-Edit 2511 LoRA which is used to prototype the style and generation methods.
For final map I used Qwen to train a Klein 4B LoRA which reproduced the style at 1/4 of the cost.
I really enjoyed this process of fine-tuning smaller open source models.If I did the map with Nano Banana 2 it would have cost around 7k USD!Credit for the idea goes to Isometric NYC.

stories.title: ‘Ahead of his time’: AI helps unlock discoveries hidden in notebooks of man who transformed maths
summary: Kurt Gödel left 1,009 pages of densely written text – much of it in an obsolete shorthand – which is now said to contain hundreds of proved theoremsThe Austrian logician Kurt Gödel was one of the most original thinkers of the 20th century.
His two incompleteness theorems, published in 1931, transformed mathematics and paved the way for the digital age.After his seminal results of the 1930s, Gödel published only a few papers.
His unpublished work, however, runs to tens of thousands of pages, and is of great interest to historians of science.
